answer: A farm must therefore either lie, which the dune graph proves on replay, or recruit 86 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the timber registry records each claim and the garden audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 72% of the attester's bond. That is 6 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
